hints: Use the gravitational potential energy formula $\Delta E_p = mgh$, where $h$ is the vertical height gained.
Relate the vertical height to the distance up the slope using trigonometry: $h = d\sin\theta = 20\sin 30^\circ$.
Substitute mass $m = 8\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and height $h$ to find the energy change.
walkthrough:
Calculate the vertical height gained by the particle moving $20\text{ m}$ up the $30^\circ$ slope:
$$h = 20\sin 30^\circ = 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ m}$$

Calculate the gain in gravitational potential energy:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 8 \times 10 \times 10 = 800\text{ J}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
The change in gravitational potential energy of an object is given by:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh$$

When moving along an inclined plane of angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ for a distance $d = 20\text{ m}$, the vertical height gained is:
$$h = d\sin\theta = 20\sin 30^\circ$$

Evaluate the sine of $30^\circ$, which is $\frac{1}{2}$:
$$h = 20 \times \frac{1}{2} = 10\text{ m}$$

Substitute $m = 8\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $h = 10\text{ m}$ into the potential energy equation:
$$\Delta E_p = 8 \times 10 \times 10 = 800\text{ J}$$

hints: The total work done against gravity and friction equals the work done against gravity (gain in potential energy) plus work done against friction: $W_{\text{total}} = \Delta E_p + W_{\text{fric}}$.
Express work done against friction as force times distance: $W_{\text{fric}} = F \times 20$.
Substitute the values into $800 + 20F = 1146$ and solve for the frictional force $F$.
walkthrough:
Set up the work equation: total work done against gravity and friction is the sum of the potential energy gained and the work against friction:
$$W_{\text{total}} = \Delta E_p + F \times d$$

Substitute $\Delta E_p = 800\text{ J}$, $d = 20\text{ m}$, and $W_{\text{total}} = 1146\text{ J}$:
$$800 + 20F = 1146$$

Solve for the frictional force $F$:
$$20F = 1146 - 800 = 346 \implies F = \frac{346}{20} = 17.3\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Work done against gravity when ascending equals the increase in gravitational potential energy, which was found in part (i) to be $800\text{ J}$:
$$W_{\text{gravity}} = 800\text{ J}$$

The work done against friction over the $20\text{ m}$ distance is force times distance:
$$W_{\text{friction}} = F \times 20 = 20F\text{ J}$$

The problem states that the total work done against gravity and friction is $1146\text{ J}$:
$$W_{\text{gravity}} + W_{\text{friction}} = 1146$$
$$800 + 20F = 1146$$

Subtract $800$ from both sides to isolate the friction term:
$$20F = 1146 - 800 = 346$$

Divide both sides by $20$ to determine $F$:
$$F = \frac{346}{20} = 17.3\text{ N}$$
